main_body: A tall church pew seen side-on: a tall brown backrest post on the left (x 0-3) and a seat body to the right with three red cushion panels stacked vertically, drawn as a flat elevation.
top_band: none; only a 2-row light brown strip (rows 14-15) at the top of the seat box, same family as the frame, and 2-row brown dividers between the red panels
evidence: The pew is drawn as an end-on or side profile: a tall backrest column beside a box with red cushion panels stacked vertically, each one a vertical face. The only 'top' is a 2px light-brown rim (rows 14-15) at the top of the seat box, which is a rim and not a surface seen from above. No seat surface is visible from above, and the column scan shows red face, brown divider, red face, brown divider, with no foreshortened horizontal band. This matches the red side-elevation chair and thin-seat examples in the guide.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 colours per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Its flat-fill coverage is 25% against 13% and 0%. The red cushions are large flat blocks with only a dark edge. The wood has 2-3 tones and no grain. The outline is a tinted dark brown (only 2% neutral), which is good, but the shading is shallow and the texture flat, so the piece looks thinner than the Beodeul references.
